skill.name: delight
skill.description: Add thoughtful micro-interactions, personality, and context-aware polish that make user interfaces more memorable without blocking usability.
skill.summary: Guides teams to add appropriate delight through animation, copy, empty states, loading states, and celebrations.
skill.author: pbakaus

content.value_statement: Functional interfaces can feel flat, forgettable, or frustrating during key moments. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code add appropriate polish through copy, animation, feedback, and celebration patterns.
actual_capabilities: Identifies natural delight moments in success, empty, loading, error, and interaction states.
Recommends context-aware delight strategies for playful, professional, quirky, or elegant products.
Suggests micro-interactions, animation patterns, sound cues, and celebration moments.
Provides copy guidance for errors, empty states, labels, tooltips, and loading messages.
Highlights accessibility, performance, reduced motion, and user fatigue considerations.
Gives quality checks for whether delight improves the user experience.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not include a runnable implementation script.
It depends on product context to choose the right tone and interaction level.
It references other design preparation steps that may not exist in every workspace.
It cannot validate real user reactions without testing or feedback.

use_cases.title: Polish onboarding flows
use_cases.description: Add welcoming empty states, first-use feedback, and progress moments that make setup feel clearer and more memorable.

use_cases.title: Improve product feedback states
use_cases.description: Create success, loading, and error states that feel useful, calm, and aligned with the brand voice.

use_cases.title: Define brand interaction personality
use_cases.description: Choose animation, copy, and visual behaviors that express the product personality without distracting from core tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Find simple delight opportunities
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner audit of one interface area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the delight skill on our empty state. Identify three small improvements that match a professional product tone.

prompt_templates.title: Refine a success moment
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate improvement for a completed user action.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the delight skill to improve the save confirmation flow. Suggest animation, copy, and accessibility safeguards.

prompt_templates.title: Design loading and error personality
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced guidance for multiple waiting and failure states.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the delight skill to create loading and error state patterns for a data dashboard. Keep the tone calm, specific, and non-distracting.

prompt_templates.title: Build a complete delight strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the delight skill to audit our product experience and propose a delight strategy across onboarding, daily workflows, achievements, and recovery moments.

output_examples.input: Improve an empty project dashboard for a professional SaaS tool.
output: A warm empty state headline that explains the next action clearly.
A subtle illustration that reflects the product domain instead of generic decoration.
A first-project completion moment with a short checkmark animation and no delay.

output_examples.input: Make a loading state feel less generic for a finance dashboard.
output: Specific progress messages about preparing reports and syncing recent transactions.
A quiet skeleton screen that preserves layout and avoids playful jokes.
Reduced-motion support and no sound by default.

output_examples.input: Add delight to a creative writing app.
output: Gentle milestone celebrations for word count goals.
Rotating encouragement that avoids repeated or distracting copy.
Small hover details on writing tools that preserve focus.

best_practices: Match every delight choice to the product domain, audience, and emotional moment.
Keep delightful moments fast, accessible, and easy to ignore or skip.
Use specific product language instead of generic playful filler.
anti_patterns: Do not delay core functionality for animation, sound, or celebration.
Do not use playful copy during serious errors or high-stakes tasks.
Do not add delight to every interaction until the interface feels noisy.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create interface polish, micro-interactions, copy, celebrations, and feedback states that feel appropriate to the product.

faq.question: Does it write production-ready UI code?
faq.answer: It provides patterns and examples, but implementation still depends on the application framework and design system.

faq.question: Can it support serious business software?
faq.answer: Yes. It emphasizes restrained, useful delight for professional contexts instead of forced playfulness.

faq.question: Does it cover accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It reminds users to respect reduced motion, avoid blocking flows, and keep delight from harming usability.

faq.question: Can it help with loading states?
faq.answer: Yes. It suggests specific loading messages, progress patterns, skeleton screens, and performance-aware waiting experiences.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
